source.title: Inconsistency-Aware Minimization: Improving Generalization with Unlabeled Data
source.authors: Hee-Sung Kim; H. Kim; Sungyoon Lee

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices; no apparent cut-off or garbling prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Measures associations between trained-network properties and the generalization gap using local inconsistency and Hessian metrics, a different measure from the specific property in V7. It also reports test-error results for a newly proposed regularizer.
record.gate_note: The paper’s background statements about memorizing random labels and cited prior studies are not its own results. IAM’s results test a new regularizer, not any listed version’s intervention; recorded under fits_no_version. Figure-only time-course findings are not assigned numerical values.
record.test_reason: The study measures local output inconsistency and unscaled Hessian curvature, and evaluates its proposed IAM regularizer. None measures V7's magnitude-aware tolerance of weight perturbations before training error rises. Its other experiments do not test V1–V6 or V8. Related generalization results alone do not establish a test of a listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that local inconsistency correlates with the generalization gap, has different empirical behavior from conventional sharpness metrics, and motivates IAM improvements in supervised, semi-supervised, and self-supervised learning. They describe supervised performance as matching or exceeding SAM; this is an overall characterization, not superiority in every condition.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces local inconsistency and IAM; the paper does not reproduce the specific interventions or measurements in V1–V8.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured associations differ by architecture and by weight-decay/data-augmentation subgroups: Hessian metrics correlate positively within WRN28-2 subgroups but negatively overall, while Sρ remains positively correlated overall. IAM results also vary with dataset, K, perturbation radius, and mini-batch configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10, local inconsistency correlates positively with the generalization gap for 6CNN (τ = 0.5141) and WRN28-2 (τ = 0.3658). Hessian trace and maximum eigenvalue correlate positively for 6CNN but negatively overall for WRN28-2, despite positive within-subgroup associations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local output inconsistency can track generalization gaps across training configurations where unscaled Hessian curvature has confounded pooled associations.

fits_no_version.finding: IAM variants reduce reported test errors against SGD across the listed supervised image-classification tasks, with outcomes varying against SAM and ASAM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularizing local output inconsistency can improve held-out classification performance under the tested, tuned training recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: From 200 to 400 ImageNet epochs, SGD Top-1 error changes from 22.66% to 22.80%, while SAM and both IAM variants improve; the 400-epoch SAM and IAM results are single runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under this ImageNet recipe, SAM and IAM benefit more from extended training than SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing IAM-D estimation steps from K = 1 to K = 5 reduces the listed standard-batch CIFAR-10 error from 3.28% to 2.98%, with running time increasing from 239 to 525 seconds per epoch.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More inner estimation steps can improve IAM-D test performance at additional computational cost.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning; PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The correlation experiment is on CIFAR-10 and two architectures; the text gives no uncertainty estimates for Kendall’s Tau. Some extended ImageNet epoch comparisons are single runs. IAM comparisons use tuned hyperparameters, and the paper notes extra computational cost.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within 60 rows, omitted individual Table 1 SAM/ASAM comparators for F-MNIST and SVHN, some duplicate ImageNet Top-1/Top-5 and epoch-specific entries, detailed IAM mini-batch-size sweeps, and semi-/self-supervised results. These appear in Sections 5.2–5.3 and Appendices E.1–E.5; none test a listed version.

untested.parts: No own experiment comparing random-label fitting and held-out performance with natural-label training.
No width sweep beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
No controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No adaptive-optimizer-versus-SGD comparison under the specified tuning conditions. AdamW baselines on different architectures do not provide that comparison.
No comparison of actual training batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets. Appendix E.1 varies perturbation sub-batch size while holding the total update batch fixed at 256.
No dropout intervention or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.

No magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance measured by training-error increases, and no ranking against norm- and margin-based measures among similarly fitted networks. Local inconsistency and unscaled Hessian metrics measure different constructs.
No identification and removal of memorized training examples followed by retraining against random-removal controls.

record.verdict_notes: Change the reader's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. Different methods qualify as T2 only when they measure the same version's question; here the central measures change the construct specified by V7. R7–R50 are method-performance comparisons or ablations and should be excluded from listed-claim evidence, though they can remain as contextual findings. Minimum-test-error reporting and SGD's selection across epoch budgets should be explicit. No additional result bearing on a listed version was found in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the specified tuning conditions.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Dropout effects and its removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing examples identified as memorized and retraining.

rows.subject: 6CNN
rows.stage_stated: trained using SGD; until convergence (< 400) epochs
rows.operation_detail: Measured local inconsistency against generalization gap across hyperparameter settings.
rows.measure: Kendall’s Tau between Sρ and generalization gap (test error - train error)
rows.note: Positive association is reported; the metric is local inconsistency, not V7’s magnitude-aware sharpness.
rows.check: The reported τ = 0.5141 concerns output KL sensitivity under an absolute Euclidean perturbation radius, not V7's magnitude-aware training-error sharpness.
